title: Six-Month Metabolic Outcomes in Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes Under Multifactorial Management: A Retrospective Cohort Study
content:
Background and Objectives: Newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is managed with lifestyle and pharmacological treatment started together. The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical and metabolic outcomes at six months in adults with newly diagnosed T2DM receiving structured therapeutic education, medical nutrition therapy and standard pharmacotherapy.
Materials and Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort, we analyzed 100 adults (aged 21–84 years) newly diagnosed with T2DM in Bucharest, Romania (2024–2025), with complete evaluations at baseline and at six months. Changes in HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, lipids, body mass index, blood pressure and renal function were assessed with paired tests; secondary analyses were exploratory.
Results: Mean age was 58.2±13.87 years; 51% were women. Obesity, hypertension and dyslipidemia were present in 63%, 72% and 63%. Mean HbA1c decreased from 8.43±2.55% to 6.47 ± 1.26% (−1.95%, 95% CI [−2.45; −1.46]), and 88% reached HbA1c < 7%. Fasting plasma glucose, body mass index, blood pressure, total and HDL cholesterol, and triglycerides also improved, whereas only 7% reached their LDL cholesterol target.
Conclusions: Diabetes self-management education combined with personalized nutritional therapy and standard pharmacological treatment was associated with improved glycemic control and several cardiometabolic parameters over six months. These findings support integrating structured therapeutic education and individualized nutritional interventions into the early management of T2DM.
